pr_title: sql/schemachanger: inject DML statements into end to end tests
pr_body:
Fixes: #83304

Previously, the declarative schema changer tests only ran DDL
statements for the schema change and had no mechanism for
determining correct behaviour if queries were run concurrently
at each phase. To address this, this patch adds a new framework
to these tests which allows us to inject DML (inserts / selects)
at various stages of a declarative schema change. This gives us
a more powerful framework for validating behaviour.

Release note: None

The first commit here can be ignored, and its a separate PR to make sure this runs stable. A PR is already open for it.

> I left a few questions/comments. Another thing is "where do we do sanity check about the assumption we made to the testdata file: 1. ordering of commands (setup -> stage-query/exec --> test); 2. no other commands after `test` commands?

There is a single assertion to enforce it:
```
		// Assert that only one test statement shows up and nothing can follow it
		// afterwards.
		require.Zero(t, numTestStmts, "only one test command per-test, "+
			"and it must be the last one.")
```

I'm less concerned about the setup order, we could also enforce that, but most likely it will be fine.

issue_context.title: sql/schemachanger: perform reads and writes against all tables in all stages
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

We have an advanced framework to test schema changes in each of the relevant phases. We should ensure that the table is safe for reading and writing during every phase of a schema change, and, ideally, we'd scrub the table after each such change. 

We may need to take some care to ensure that any writes don't violate any constraints unintentionally.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

We should augment the `cumulative` data-driven test framework to perform operations on the table at each stage.


Jira issue: CRDB-16985
comments: @fqazi I believe we spoke about this in our last 1:1. I'm going to tentatively put this on your plate for July.

review_comments: nit: let's add a comment here that says something along the line of "a stageKeyEntry captures the stage range in which statement(s) is to be executed"

okay, so we have essentially two layers here -- end-to-end and cumulative. Cumulative is the foundational layer that all the "high-level" testing will invoke: end-to-end, rollback, pause-resume, backup-restore. You put this `stage-exec`/`stage-query` logic here in the cumulative layer, and that means we are going to inject stmts in all the "high-level" testings, is this right? (if so, that'd be great! It's so cool to say that "we are injecting DML stms while running a DDL statement while doing backup/restore)

By putting the rewrite logic here, you also say "the rewrite for `stage-query` is responsible in the cumulative layer, while the rewrite for the `test` stmt in the testdata file is responsible in the end-to-end layer". Is this right? If so, I think this makes sense since the expected output for the `test` command is only used/concerned in the end-to-end test.

I didn't understand this part. I wanted to figure out how "--rewrite" works: If I now run the EndToEndSideEffect test with a `--rewrite` flag, what will happen? You said we will ignore those commands in EndToEndSideEffect tests, then shouldn't that nothing happens?

So, the way the rewrite works is that on the first execution of the injection tests we will gather the expected output mapped by filename + line number. On the second output, this stored output will be returned so that the data driven test can do a rewrite.
where is the "default" clause for this switch block?
can you add some comment about how we use two-pass to handle the introduction of `exec-stage` and `exec-query` here?
see my comments below; I think it's just one pass; the second pass is needed if `--rewrite`. In any case, please add some comments about this behavior somewhere. Thank you!
